record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.context_brief: Algorithms for equitable colouring under Ore bounds
record.original_question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs an equitable k-colouring of any graph G whose maximum Ore degree θ(G)=max{d(x)+d(y):xy∈E(G)} satisfies θ(G)<2k?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Is there a polynomial algorithm for constructing an equitable k-coloring of any graph G with θ(G) < 2k?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$, write $d(v)$ for the degree of a vertex $v$, and define the maximum Ore degree of $G$ by
$$\theta(G) \;=\; \max\{\, d(x)+d(y) : xy \in E(G)\,\}.$$
A proper $k$-colouring of $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ into $k$ independent sets (colour classes); it is called equitable if any two colour classes differ in size by at most $1$.

It is known that every graph $G$ with $\theta(G) < 2k$ admits an equitable $k$-colouring. The problem is the algorithmic version:

Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input a graph $G$ and an integer $k$ with $\theta(G) < 2k$, outputs an equitable $k$-colouring of $G$ in time polynomial in $|V(G)|$ and $k$?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 survey by Kierstead on equitable coloring lists this as an open conjecture: while it is proved that every graph with Ore-degree θ(G) < 2k admits an equitable k-coloring, the existing proof gives only an exponential-time algorithm, and the existence of a polynomial-time algorithm in full generality remains open. Partial progress exists for sufficiently large graphs with k linear in |G|.

status_evidence.title: Results and Problems on Equitable Coloring of Graphs (Kierstead)
status_evidence.snippet: Because of the repeated use of Lemma 7, this proof only yields an exponential-time algorithm. ... Conjecture: There is a polynomial-time algorithm for finding an equitable k-coloring of every graph with maximum Ore-degree Θ(G)<2k.
status_evidence.claim: The polynomial-time algorithmic version is stated as an open conjecture; the known proof is only exponential-time.

status_evidence.title: A step toward Chen-Lih-Wu conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: For a graph G with d(x)+d(y) < 2k for all xy in E(G), there exists a polynomial-time algorithm to determine an equitable k-coloring for G when |G| is sufficiently large and k is linear with respect to |G|.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: polynomial-time algorithm known under additional size/linearity assumptions.
